step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Identify nodes visible on the whiteboard:
   - 'DATA SOURCES': External third-party data providers -> 'ThirdParty'
   - 'CONSUMERS': End users / underwriters accessing the platform -> 'UserConsumerWeb'
   - 'ELB': AWS Elastic Load Balancing -> 'ELB'
   - 'K8S': Kubernetes cluster running on EC2 compute (with Keycloak, Jupyter, Kong) -> 'EC2'
   - 'MQ': Amazon MQ for asynchronous message queuing -> 'AmazonMQ'
   - 'VPC PEERING': VPC Peering connection -> 'VPCPeering'
   - 'MONGODB ATLAS': Hosted MongoDB Atlas database -> 'MongoDBAtlas'
   - 'RDS': Relational Database Service (PostgreSQL) -> 'RDS'
   - 'REDIS': Redis caching layer -> 'ElastiCache'

2. Trace physical arrows (edges):
   - 'DATA SOURCES' (ThirdParty) -> 'ELB'
   - 'ELB' -> 'K8S' (EC2)
   - 'CONSUMERS' (UserConsumerWeb) -> 'K8S' (EC2)
   - 'K8S' (EC2) -> 'MQ' (AmazonMQ) and 'MQ' (AmazonMQ) -> 'K8S' (EC2) (bidirectional arrow drawn)
   - 'K8S' (EC2) -> 'VPC PEERING' (VPCPeering)
   - 'VPC PEERING' (VPCPeering) -> 'MONGODB ATLAS' (MongoDBAtlas)
   - 'MONGODB ATLAS' (MongoDBAtlas) -> 'K8S' (EC2) (curved return arrow drawn from MongoDB back to K8S)

graph.name: Intellect Design - Fabric Data Service Architecture
graph.notes: Architecture showing data ingestion from external sources via ELB into a K8S cluster on EC2, decoupled via Amazon MQ, and using MongoDB Atlas via VPC Peering alongside RDS and Redis.

nodes.name: Data Sources
nodes.notes: External data sources including social media, regulatory data, and premium connectors

nodes.name: Consumers
nodes.notes: Underwriters, policy agents, and insurance carriers

nodes.name: ELB
nodes.notes: Elastic Load Balancer fanning out crawled/connected data

nodes.name: K8S Cluster
nodes.notes: Kubernetes cluster hosting microservices, Keycloak, Jupyter Notebooks, and Kong API Gateway

nodes.name: MQ
nodes.notes: Amazon MQ for message buffering and asynchronous processing

nodes.name: VPC Peering
nodes.notes: VPC Peering connection for private network access to MongoDB Atlas

nodes.name: MongoDB Atlas
nodes.notes: Primary database storing processed entity and risk analysis data

nodes.name: RDS
nodes.notes: Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL used by Kong API Gateway and Keycloak

nodes.name: REDIS
nodes.notes: Redis for session management and cache across microservices

edges.notes: Data ingested from external data sources into ELB
ELB fans out data into K8S microservices
K8S microservices push messages into Amazon MQ
K8S pipeline consumes messages from Amazon MQ for ML processing
Processed data sent via VPC Peering
VPC Peering routes data to MongoDB Atlas
Query results returned from MongoDB Atlas to K8S
Consumers make API requests to Kong API Gateway running in K8S
